utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to give me another session so that we go through all of the statements made by this witness. This is not a question. This is a request. Did you not say in paragraph 11 -- I'm going to read it in English: [In English] "The Municipal Crisis Staff of which I was a member was involved in working on manning the police reserve formation and later on working on the recruiting people into the new TO unit. In cooperation with the Municipal Crisis Staff I was engaged in acquisition of weapons for the settlement of Svrake, Semizovac --"

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, these questions were all dealt with with the witness yesterday. I don't know why Mr. Karadzic wants to go back over them again today, if he has very limited time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is whether it is true that you had dugouts where you hid these weapons.

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no dugouts and we did not have any special weapons that we were supposed to hide in dugouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But then we'll have to call up a document, a record of when you were heard as a witness on the 15th of March, 1993. The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina versus yours truly. ERN page number -- I'll have to rely on that, 00287259. This is what you say. Some hunting weapons that we had we hid in bunkers, dugouts and cellars. Did you have them all on the 2nd of May?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Every house, or most houses, in my neighbourhood had certain basements. We didn't have any bunkers. Bunkers are special establishments that have to be built. Now, in addition to housing facilities, whether someone had dug out a trench or a small dugout or something to protect oneself from gunfire that was aimed at our village for months, it is possible that that kind of thing existed. But it wasn't that these were specific dugouts for hiding weapons that we didn't even have, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean, witness, that we should not take your statements verbatim?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland? Did you find the reference?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 65 ter number 22195 is the statement of the 25th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us upload it and show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, a moment ago when I made a reference to Mr. Karadzic having very limited time, that's his understanding, it's not the OTP's. He's had over four hours with this witness already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where can we see his reference to bunkers --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Page 3 of the English translation and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2 of Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that, may I explain. Today the witness said that he had not been informed about what the MUP had been informed about. This is what I read from his statement and it shows that he cooperated with the MUP. And also what I said, that he was buying and procuring weapons, and then he says that they only had hunting guns. Ah, yes, now I'm going to read it. It's the end of the second paragraph, Witness. The end of the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in English, could you also get the English version for the other participants?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At this moment, I don't think the English translation has been uploaded. But let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The end of the second paragraph, you say, "Near your village -- or, rather, the military facility of Semizovac fire was opened at our village and for two days we put up some resistance with the few hunting weapons we had. We hid in dugouts, shelters, and bunkers -- or, rather, basements." If that was not the case, can we not take your statements verbatim?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, you cannot say that you cannot take my statements as such. This is in context. When you're fired at, you have to hide somewhere. I mean bunkers and dugouts, as I say here, it's sort of makeshift bunkers. It's not those that were fortified by concrete. Before that, during the attacks, people were digging dugouts to protect themselves from the fire that was coming at them. And that is what you can establish on the basis of this statement. It is true that we were seeking shelter before fire. But in your previous question, when you asked about bunkers, dugouts and cellars, it seems that we had enormous quantities of weapons that we were hiding in basements, bunkers, and dugouts. After all, if there was combat activity going on, we wouldn't be hiding weapons. We would be using it, possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, after escaping, on the 5th of December, 1992, did you join the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina again? You can say "yes" or "no" now.

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: After my escape from prison, I did join the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Army of Republika Srpska, the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, did they make it possible for you to see your mother in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't this Sarajevo Romanija Corps that made it possible for me. This happened in a very roundabout way. Before the war, my mother was treated in the Kasindol hospital. After I escaped from the camp, with the assistance of the local Red Cross and with the assistance of the International Red Cross, I managed to transfer my mother from the Kasindol hospital to Sarajevo where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This will also require only a "yes" or "no" answer. Does the Kasindol hospital belong to the area of Sarajevo under Serb control?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under Serb control.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3353, could I have that now, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm actually having trouble with LiveNote. I can't scroll back up to the transcript. I don't know if that can be fixed by the technicians. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One way of resolving is to restart but, okay, no doubt the technician will look into the matter. I have no problem with mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, this is the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska addressed to the command of the Sarajevo Romanija and Drina Corps, dated the 25th of November, 1993. Can we now look at the next page? And it reads as follows: "On Sarajevo-Grbavica road, and then via Pale towards Belgrade, the following reunion of the people with their family will take place. Number 1, Muracevic, Rabija and her son Muracevic, Eset," and now the remaining names are Croatian and Muslim respectively. And it was signed by Major-General Manojlo Milovanovic, the Chief of Staff. So he's giving permission to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps to enable you to reunite with your mother. Is that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: That is when my mother was exchanged. With the assistance of the ICRC, my mother was transferred from Kasindol hospital to Sarajevo where I lived. It is true that that is when my mother was transferred to the part of Sarajevo which was under the control of the BH Army, and she joined me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You, as her son, Eset Muracevic, you said that she was exchanged. What did the Serbs gets in exchange for her?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you, with the aid of the ICRC, my mother was reunited with me and she came to live with me. I have no information as to what preceded that and what was the response of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The only detail I knew was that with the assistance of the Red Cross, my mother would be transferred and that is what happened. But I didn't have an opportunity to see this document. Maybe it was hidden somewhere in the piles of documents, and I see some signatures here. I was offered at the time of reunification to sign some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, let's go on. Your mother remained living in the Serbian territory while you were in captivity. Then she was treated in a Serbian hospital, and then, in November of 1993, at your request, she was released and she reunited with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother was supposed to be placed at the clinical centre in Kosevo to receive treatment. However, due to some prior treatments that he [as interpreted] had received in Kasindol, that is why she was put up there. She stayed in that hospital, according to her words, and she wasn't maltreated by anyone there because she was an elderly person who suffered from high blood pressure and diabetes. According to what she said after reunification, she had not had any significant problems, apart from the fact that she was worried that no family members came to visit her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1111, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have now to move to an important document, and if the Trial Chamber allows me, on some other occasion, we are going to demonstrate a whole number of incongruities that occurred in the statements given by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, did you bring with you or did you provide a list here - can we have 1D3334? - a list of citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina killed in Vogosca by the aggressor army?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: That's part of the list that was provided in a sort of way, as part of my statements. However, the final number that I reached of the people killed in Vogosca municipality that were under the control of the Serbian authorities was 294. Those people were either killed or taken to an undisclosed location. Many of them passed before that through the camps, Planjo's house and the garage and bunker, and some were killed in their villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's stick to the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Since we do not have the English translation, could you kindly read the first two lines, including the title, Mr. Muracevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is one of the lists of the people killed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you kindly read the document so that we can hear the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "List of the citizens who, during the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the period 1992/1995, were killed in Vogosca by the aggressor army, the army of Bosnian Serbs, and whose burial places are not known."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are now going to demonstrate that these people that have numbers next to them, at least those people, but not only them, we identified with the assistance of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as people who rejoined the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and were subsequently killed in combat. The list that we received from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is 1D3355. If we can have this list on the other half of the screen, so 1D3355. I'm going to read now. Adnan Puris, killed in combat, and is listed under number 50 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we are experiencing some technical difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to break for ten minutes. --- Break taken at 11.43 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karadzic, you will have 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I think -- I think I would have even more than 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Maybe 20 minutes but not more than that, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the participants please look on the right-hand side of the screens? The Republican Centre for Investigation of War Crimes is informing us in February of this year that there was a list attached to this letter that had already been provided to The Hague Tribunal. I'm going to read this letter: "Attached herewith please find the list in electronic form provided at your request referring to members of the BH Army killed during the war in 1992/1995. This list had previously been provided to The Hague Tribunal, and the Hague Tribunal placed these lists at the disposal of the Commission for Srebrenica of the government of Republika Srpska and the archives of the commission are stored in the Republican Centre for Investigation of War Crimes." Number 1, I'm not sure if this list has been disclosed, and secondly, can we have the -- this list, 1D3348? We need both the list that we saw earlier and the one which is listed as 1D3348. This one is okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's all right. We have both lists. Can we now find page 543 in e-court on the left-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 453.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, you said killed by the aggressor army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we have 1D3334 and next to it 1D3348, and then within 1D3348 we need page 453 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say, and this list has been introduced through you, claiming that these people were killed. Do you make a distinction in our language between dying and getting killed?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, on the left-hand side of the screen we see the list of members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and on the right-hand side is the list that I provided of the people who were killed in the territory under your control. The left-hand side list treats people who, in a way, regulated their status as members of the armed forces. So in this list, it is not shown the circumstances of their death. The people listed on the right-hand side of the screen are people who were in Vogosca under the Serbian control and they were either detained on the premises where I was kept, such as Planjo's house, the garage and the bunker, or were taken away from their homes and executed in a way. So the list that I provided contains the names of the people killed in the territory controlled by the local Serbs. At the time when these people were killed, they were not killed as members of any armed formation of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, meaning that they were not members of a unit that was attacking the local Serbs. They were -- they lost their lives as prisoners, people who didn't have weapons, and were in the territory under your control. Most probably depending on the degree of their engagement before taken prisoner, whether they were in the reserve police or the regular police, their families probably had an opportunity to regulate their status as members of the armed forces, and the list that you are showing on the left-hand side of the screen shows the people whose families managed to regulate their status as members of the armed forces. They were killed, though, in the territory under the Serb control but they were not killed carrying weapons or a rifle but, rather, as unarmed people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please keep your answers short. Are you saying that Adnan Puris was killed in Vogosca as a prisoner? If the answer is yes, can you tell us where and when?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came here, I provided a list. I don't know if it was given to you as well. It contains the names of 294 people who perished in the territory under the Serb control. Maybe we can call up some of those documents because this particular list contains the details as to the place and date of their demise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that Ibrahim Brkic was killed as a prisoner or was he killed as a combatant?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not as a combatant. He was killed as someone who had been detained in the territory under the Serb control. So he was not killed as a combatant who was engaged in fighting with a rifle in his hand but, rather, killed in the territory held by the Serbs and he was not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was Adnan Puris killed? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: 294 people who --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When was Adnan Puris killed?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't ask me to give you such details off the top of my head about nearly 300 people. If you would allow me to see and look at this list, I can give you this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could the participants look at the number 50291, Adnan Puris, born in Foca, lived in Vogosca, killed on the 21st of February, 1991. "A" means "army." Killed. Not a civilian. He was killed. He wasn't murdered. You say that the family here of the late Adnan Puris was smuggling something. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: You're showing the list of persons on the left-hand side of persons who were killed while they were in the armed forces. Adnan Puris definitely was killed in the territory of Vogosca, which was under the control of your forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When and where?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we can call up the document that I brought with me. I don't know if you've been provided that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I hope that we will get the document that you brought. I don't have it. I wasn't given it. But let's move on to the next thing, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This was provided to Mr. Karadzic with the proofing note. It's document number 13 which was attached to the note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By the way, can you zoom in on the left document so that we can read the columns? The titles and the column. Can you show the first column, the first row? Could you read the column for our benefit? Because we don't have the English translation, Mr. Muracevic. Could you read -- one by one.

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: First column is RB, I assume that that means ordinal number. Next is last name, then name of the parents. Then the first name. Then JMBG, unique identification number. Then municipality of birth, municipality of residence, date of death, and ethnicity. And the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you read the first column underneath cause of death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says "Poginuo," "killed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the person we saw, Adnan Puris -- I'm sorry, let me find it, yes, Puris, Adnan Puris, died when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the 21st of February, 1995, according to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: According to this. And you wanted to take a look at your documents that you brought with you? Let's revert to the previous setting so that we can see the first name, Adnan Puris. Do you have it with you, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Reid is uploading it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Karadzic, please continue in the meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to recommend to the participants, first of all a piece of information. This left-hand list was given to the Army of Republika Srpska by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in a mutual exchange of information about those who were killed. So I would like to draw everyone's attention to column "Belongingness" or "Membership," where we have the letters, A and P. Army, police and unknown. And the column "Cause of death," there is killed and unknown. So "N" is "unknown" and "Poginuo" is "killed." Can all the parties now, as soon as the documents are uploaded, to look at the left-handed number on the right-hand list and that is the number according -- under which the person is in the left list, in the records of members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina who were killed. Can we look at the following page of the list on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these members from Arab countries listed under 61 to 65, Mr. Muracevic?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they come from Arab countries, but the documents that were found in the municipal building, these -- this was marked by the Army of Republika Srpska that these people were killed in that period, in that area. I don't know who these people are. They were killed in the area held by the local Serbs. I don't know who they were. They were not brought to the facilities where I was detained. I found their names in the part of the documentation that we found after the 23rd of February, 1996, when we entered this part of the area. And we found that among the documents that were left behind by the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, bear it in mind that the Chamber does not have the English translation of this. So first thing you should do is to ask the witness to read the handwritten part so that we can follow. And whose handwriting it was. And then put such questions. Could you read out what is written in by hand there, Mr. Muracevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the list that I provided, somebody added the numbers and specifically two, four, the five last names that are circled, these are the names Majrem Abu, Maris Abu, Imran Abu, Muraj Aub, and Talha Abu. Somebody added in handwriting next to those names, "Who are these Arabs?" I don't know who added that. It was probably somebody from Mr. Karadzic's Defence. They might have marked that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Muracevic. Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the point I was going to make. The document did not have any of the numbers written down the side when it was -- when the witness provided it to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Or the comment next to the names 61 to 65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you agree that those comments, the note, has been made by the Defence? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. On the left-hand side, the Defence put in the numbers under which these are listed in the list given to us by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As for this, "Who are these Arabs," it was probably an investigator from the Defence. These Arabs are not on the list of the Armija dead soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, who drafted this list, who compiled the list that you brought?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: The list that we are looking at on the right-hand side is a list that I made on the basis of my personal information and on the basis of documents we found in the territory when we entered it on the 23rd of February, 1996, that was left behind by the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to this, it turns out that the Serbs captured these six Arabs, held them and killed them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documentation that I was able to see, all the documentation says is that they were killed on a specific day in the Vogosca territory, but we couldn't decipher whether they were captured or whether they were liquidated somewhere, killed. I don't know. There were no circumstances listed as to how they died.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D335 now, please, on the right-hand side? 1D3335.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I note for the record that the markings made on this document were not there when it was provided by the witness, so presumably the Defence have also made those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic has agreed with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Muracevic, to read the text that is above the names?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: So we are talking about the document that is shown on the right-hand of the screen and it is titled, "List of citizens who during the aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992 to 1995 were captured by the aggressor soldiers, the Bosnian Serb army, detained at their camp in Vogosca, and from there taken in an unidentified direction."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at -- can we look at 5031, let's say. Hajrudin Raonic Hajco, 50301. Hajrudin Raonic Hajco, what do they say for 50301? Killed on the 16th of June, 1992. Here it is, 50301, Hajrudin, son of Rifet Raonic. Vogosca, born in Vogosca, lived, killed on the 16th of June, 1992, a member of the army. You say that he was a prisoner. Where was he a prisoner? Are you also trying to say that this family also was messing with information?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, on the left-hand side, there is the list of persons whose families did manage to resolve for their missing and killed and get the status for them as members of the armed forces. On the right-hand list, all the persons who are on the right-hand list were captured, detained by the Serbs in the Vogosca municipality area that you were controlling. Specifically when you are talking about Hajco Hajrudin Raonic, that was one of the persons who was taken from the Planina Kuca camp in Svrake in June 1992 by representatives of the Serbian army, taken in an unidentified direction, and that was when this person was taken from this camp and has not been heard of since. We don't know of his fate to this very day. His body was never found, and he's still on the list of missing persons from the village of Svrake. The list also has Hasan Abaz under number 1, who was tortured horrifically in the camp. He was beaten, made to somersault on his head from a height of three metres. He was exposed to homosexual relations, he was forced into homosexual relations with other prisoners, and in June 1992, this person was taken with a group of 28 Svrake citizens from Naka's garage in an unidentified direction and we have not learned of their fate to this very day. Most of these people here, their fate is unknown. In the meantime, some of their bodies have been exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, were you captured, just briefly, were you captured and detained?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I was detained by the Serbian army. I was taken to the barracks camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. We know all of that. If you had been killed after 1993, would you be listed as missing or would you be listed as somebody who was killed?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: In the legal structures of the authority of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I would be listed as unofficial in the local commune of a certain municipality, and probably my family would have tried to get me the status of a member of the army because members of the TO, the police, and the reserve forces, even if they were killed in detention camp, were considered as members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think now it's time for you to conclude your cross-examination. We'll deal with the documents but come to your last questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, you claim that this list on the left-hand side, which is an official document of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and where the status is killed, unknown, succumbed to injuries or wounds, are you saying that list is incorrect and that what -- the list that you brought you are saying that is correct and that we should not be taking into account this list on the left-hand side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: The list that you are talking about on the left-hand side is a list of names of people whose families, regardless of the fact that these men were captured and detained, their families, because these people were either members of the reserve forces, the Territorial Defence or of the police forces, secured for them the status of members of the army. So this is a list of persons whose families managed to obtain for them the status of members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina regardless of the circumstances of how they really died. The list on the left-hand side are -- on the right-hand side is a list of persons who were killed, taken away in an unidentified direction, by Bosnian Serbs, and at the point of -- in time when they were killed or when they died in a different way, they were not part of the armed formations. They were simply unarmed prisoners who were at the time held by the Serbian forces in camps such as Nakina Kuca, the bunker, Planjo's garage, and other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Muracevic, do you have any proof that things are the way you say or should we just take your word for it?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the witness has answered the question already. Whether you challenge it, whether it's correct or not, it is subject of your further submission, but don't argue with the witness. The witness said that on the left table -- side list, it is not shown the circumstances of their death. So it -- let's move on. Or it's time to conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I think, witness, sir, that these are dangerous lies that insult these victims and these families, "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I cannot understand this remark of yours. It is your intention to use this court to intimidate me and to make me forget what I experienced. On the right-hand side of the screen are listed persons who were in detention in captivity in camps by members of the Army of Republika Srpska. They were taken away, killed, or taken away in an unidentified direction from their places of captivity. And, for example, if we look at Alic, Enes, or any of these people have in the meantime been exhumed. Their bodies have been exhumed. We have exhumed a certain number, three persons, down river from that particular camp. It was some ten kilometres downstream from Svrake. That's where their bodies were exhumed. The other option was that all of these people on the right-hand side were captured in the places where I was, bunker, Planina Kuca, Naka's garage, they were in house detention, and sometimes we were would pass through areas where members of the Serbian army were keeping these persons captive. At the point in time when they died, at their time of death, they were not part of any armed formations. They were simply persons who were being held as prisoners, as detainees, or I don't know how else to describe them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. Can these three lists be tendered, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we have seen four documents. First 1D3334, 1D3334 and 1D3335, list A and B. And a letter of confirmation, 1D3355, and finally the list, 1D3348. Are you tendering all of them? Shall we mark them for identification pending translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, 1D3334 and 1D3335, we have read into the record the headings on the top of the document so I think they can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ah, yes. Yes. We can admit those two documents without having to wait for the English translation because we can read them all. So we will admit them, those two documents, with the caveat that notations made on these documents were made by the Defence team. And in the meanwhile, we'll mark for identification 1D3348 and 1D3355. Shall we give the numbers? The list of people -- only the columns can be -- should be translated not all the names. So just the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that has been translated as well. So we can admit that list as well, which is 1D3348. It is document of 700 pages, more than 700 pages, yes. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The only thing, Your Honour, we would need to know what these other things stand for in the final column because I see some Ns and then some abbreviations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we heard what "poginuo" means. And we heard these Defence submission what N means and then --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does "PODO.US.R" mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we have the assistance from the interpreters? PODO --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may help, I assume that that means succumbed to injuries or wounds, so wounded and then died later. "N" can be "nepoznato," "unknown," or "nestao," "missing." "Poginuo" means killed in fighting. "Ubijen" means "executed." Membership, "A" is "army," "P" is "police," so that means that there are no civilians on this list. There are only members of the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sutherland, do you have much for redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, maybe 15 or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder whether we need to take a break or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Maybe 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then it's safe to have a break. When did we resume? Since they haven't changed the tape we have to take a break now. Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just deal with the last document we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, may I interrupt you for just a brief while to assist us in a very, very small matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Baird.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And can I refer you to the statement of the witness, the amalgamated statement, at para 13. The attack on Svrake, para 13. You have it there? The line, "People were wounded and killed." Now, the conjunction "and" there is joining two sentences, is it not? People were wounded and people were killed? You agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Well, now, you referred to us footnote 49, and you said in his statement of 1996, he said that four people were wounded and one killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I mean, you know, they aren't the same, are they? People were wounded on the one hand and one -- and killed, on the one hand, and one was killed, on the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: What then would you want the Chamber to consider, if, for instance, it's addressing the issue of conflicting previous statements? Which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has clarified that the word -- that one person was killed and that's on the record. So the sentence now reads, "People were wounded and one killed." In fact, he said that four people were wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: All right. So therefore --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Because the -- the footnotes to this statement are not in evidence. It's simply the amalgamated witness statement is and the footnotes are to assist the Defence if they want to go back to find where the information that -- where we have drawn the information from in compiling the amalgamated witness statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- and he can see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: So therefore when it reads, "People were killed," we should not take it literally as people, meaning more than one person was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, people were wounded and one person was killed. I take the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And one person was killed. That is how we should approach it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We haven't given the number for the last four exhibits. Shall we do that now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 1D3355 will be MFI D1112. 1D3334 will be D1113. 1D3335 will be D1114. And 1D3348 will be D1115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, at one point in time, did you or did you not say that, in the meantime, you are going to produce all the inconsistent parts of various witness statements made by -- this witness? I'm trying to find that part. Did you say so?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Sorry, I'm waiting for the interpretation. [In English] I'm waiting for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But in order to do so, do you not need to tender all the witness statements?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? May I say what my idea was? I wanted to seek leave to make this comparison and to tender these pages. Not necessarily the entire material. There are about 15 or 20 testimonies and statements. Had they all been admitted, I would be able to deal with it in my closing arguments but this way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is not in the evidence we cannot look at it. So that's why I turned to Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it's unfortunate that he did not have enough time to do this correctly so that we could have presented them to the witness and gotten their comment -- his comment on them. But if you're minded to receive the statements, we would think that that's a good solution, given the lack of time to use to -- for traditional impeachment methods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I disagree. I think that the witness -- any inconsistencies that Mr. Karadzic deems in his prior statements, should be put to the witness that he has an opportunity to explain them. And not simply after he's left the Tribunal to then produce a document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Then I need time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We agree with you, Ms. Sutherland. Now he's your witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Does it mean that I am going to get time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just on D1115 that's just been admitted, the list of persons, the big long list, Mr. Karadzic asserted that the word "poginuo," apologies for my pronunciation of it, p-o-g-i-n-u-o, means "killed in fighting." In fact, it's our understanding that that word simply means "killed" and it can be a death caused by unnatural causes or any other form of death, but simply, it doesn't mean "killed in fighting."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That has been noted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We would invite the Chamber to seek input from CLSS in relation to that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we ask just the first page of that document to be translated, to be safe. Thank you. That can be done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we are waiting, "ubijen" and "poginuo" mean completely different things. If somebody is "ubijen," "killed," and if he is a member of an army, although even if he were not to be killed in combat, if he loses his life, the status of his death remains the same, and his family is entitled to the same rights, if he is a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All those are matters to be discussed in the submission and to be clarified by the language expert. But this is not the time to discuss it further. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, this afternoon, earlier today, at page 50, Mr. Karadzic was taking -- was -- took you to one of the lists that you had provided, a list of citizens killed, and you said that: "That list was provided as part of my statements. However, the final number that I reached of people killed in Vogosca municipality that were under the control of the Serbian authorities was 294." First of all, that list, the earlier list, that was up on the screen, that was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2001, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can have on the screen 65 ter number 23 -- sorry, 90236, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document that's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this was a list of 294 persons, and this list you provided to the Prosecution when you came to The Hague on the weekend; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is this the list that you were referring to earlier in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When did you prepare this list?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: This list was created from the moment I was detained until I walked into this courtroom. So we can take it until the present day. That is to say that it was compiled on the basis of information that was compiled after the war as well. This list does include a large number of people who were in bunker, Planjo's house and other locations where they were detained. They were taken from their homes and then they suffered in the occupied part of the territory of Vogosca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And when you say this list was compiled from when you were first detained until -- until today, if I understand you, does -- well, does that mean that you're updating this list as we go or as -- as you obtain further information in relation to exhumations, for example?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Every new bit of knowledge that came after the exhumations and after we found out about what happened to missing persons meant that people were added to this list. It is not a final or finite list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could just go to the last page, please, page 19, and that is, I think, what you say at the bottom of the document, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's right. This is a list of names, and then on the basis of exhumations or relevant witness statements, these are persons who may be considered to have lost their lives in Serb-controlled territory in the Vogosca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When you say witness statements, are you referring to people coming to you in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to persons who were detained together with me in some of the camps or in the period when the territory of the municipality of Vogosca was under Serb control, they lived in that territory. When the war was over in 1995, when we entered the area, we found about 100 inhabitants who were ethnic Muslims and who spent almost the entire war in that area. In most cases these were families that involved mixed marriages and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it was those people that provided with you the information?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: From these people, on the basis of personal knowledge, and also in view of persons who spent some time with persons who had been killed or who went missing from a certain area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'd seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have to put it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, until we have the document translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does the Trial Chamber allow the Defence to put a mark next to every one of these names of the persons who are on this list denoting the nature of these deaths? So can we bar table that kind of a document so that the Trial Chamber would know what this was all about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll deal with that when it is filed. I can't -- I'm not in the position to give an answer to that question without knowing what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document was disclosed to the Defence, so they may well have used it in cross-examination if they wished to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will give that an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P2397.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? Just one word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to spare Madam Sutherland of this remark of mine. This was disclosed at the very last moment and I've just seen it now. I think that we got it on Monday, while I was busy with other witnesses, so at the very last moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is on the record that the witness brought it on the weekend and it was disclosed on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On pages 24 and 25 today, Mr. Karadzic asked you a question in relation to was it a matter of personal revenge of things being -- happening to you in relation to the bunker, and the detention facilities. And in your answer you said, quite simply, it was something coordinated that was done by the local Serbs, and then you went on to refer to a document by Jovan Tintor. And Mr. Karadzic said do you agree, should we look for a document that Jovan Tintor had this building handed over, and you said, no, it was earlier in May and then sometime in mid-July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 01509 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is a document that you brought on the weekend, however, it has been an exhibit in -- a 65 ter exhibit in this case for some time. But in relation to the document, is this the document that you were referring to earlier today?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the document that I mentioned, and that shows that Jovan Tintor, as president of the Crisis Staff, ordered the owner of the Kontiki bed and breakfast and her son to make available these premises for interrogating detained persons. That is to say that before the attack on my village, they planned certain activities and they realised that they needed premises for interrogating persons brought in.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2398, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Muracevic, the document --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, just one observation? This was not issued by Tintor. It was issued by some deputy of his. And secondly, it is the civilian authorities that are requisitioning property and handing it over to the police. We are not dealing with this in any other way but just saying this, but what the witness said is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can make your submission later on. We all can read.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the later document you referred to, Mr. Muracevic, I will not bring up on to the screen. It's already an exhibit in this case. Yesterday, you were asked about your experiences, about documents, certain documents, that Mr. Karadzic was mistaken when he was assuming that you reviewed certain documents given to you by the state commission, and you clarified that and said that it was documents that you found in the Vogosca municipality and that you had provided to them. But then you also went on to say that -- that you did have an opportunity to review an -- an audio tape in relation to a speech that Karadzic had made. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember. The documents that we are referring to, we found after the reintegration of the Vogosca area into the federation area, after the 23rd of February 1996. And most of these documents, I can say almost all the documents, that have been presented today and as part of my statements, are documents that we found either in the municipal building in Vogosca or in some other facilities that were before that under the control of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, if I can pause you there, if I could -- I want you to look at a document now to see whether this is, in fact, the audio recording that you referred to in your transcript yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I could have Exhibit P00958, please. And if we could see page 6 of the English translation and --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I'm going to object to this now as going outside of the scope of the cross-examination, and this really should have been -- if this was important to the Prosecution, a speech of Dr. Karadzic, it should have been put to the witness on direct examination. But to bring it up now and deny us the opportunity for questioning, I think, is unfair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, could you tell us how it is transpired -- it transpired from the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Because Mr. Karadzic was putting to the witness that he was provided all these documents by the authorities, and then he was going on to say that -- well, I can do it another way, Your Honour. In relation to -- he went further on, there was a discussion further on, in relation to the selling of the land, not being able to be sold to Muslims, and that's at -- on page 12687 and 12688. The witness made reference to the fact that 215 citizens of Serb ethnicity, in relation to the municipality of Vogosca, where there were representatives of Bosniaks, Serbs and Croats, they sent a petition actually to this Vogosca Municipal Assembly to ask for banning of sale of Serb houses to Muslims and not to prohibit Muslims from building houses in that village. If I could have 65 ter number 90235 on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask for Madam Sutherland to let us know exactly what this document is? The Chamber doesn't know what this document is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document that's on the screen is a transcript of a speech by Mr. Karadzic in relation to the plebiscite of the Serb people in November 1991, which was what was referred to by the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was it given?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is not used at this moment. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic. She is not using this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I may come back to it, Your Honour. In relation to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, did you write a book?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wrote a book, "The killed and missing victims of crimes in the Vogosca municipality area in the period from 1992 to 1995." There is an excerpt from that book of mine that we can see on the screen, where I talked about a part of a statement by Mr. Karadzic around the time of the plebiscite, when he addressed a meeting, and then in the footnote, you can see that the source for that is the bulletin of the state commission for compiling facts about war crimes on the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In further text, the bulletin. And that contains all the information that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And when you mentioned this in your testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think this is just another way of getting in the same topic which we again say is beyond the scope of the cross-examination. Whether it's the speech directly or his writing about the speech on some other occasions, it's the same thing. So we maintain our objection. I wonder also if Ms. Sutherland could advise us of when this was disclosed to us? We don't seem to recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This was disclosed pursuant to Rule 66(B) in -- I will find the date. Your Honour, if I may respond to Mr. Robinson, this is not simply a way of getting these documents in through another way. I am showing during the cross-examination, and I should have been more clear, Mr. Karadzic, this witness, they were talking about Karadzic's speech, and where he said that land should not be sold to Muslims, and the witness mentioned a document that he had seen that was a petition of 215. And Mr. Karadzic said, "Have you seen this -- where is this in your previous statements?" And he said, "I have said it before several times." I am simply taking the witness to -- to his book to show that he did mention it in 2002, and we actually have the petition of 215, which I would like to exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But I simply wanted to take the witness to his book first to see if he would recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the petition I think is -- very clearly comes out of the cross-examination but Dr. Karadzic's speech does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask for another clarification of when the book was disclosed to me? If the witness has written a book, the Defence should have had the book. Secondly --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The book was disclosed to Mr. Karadzic on the 13th of October, 2009.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the second question, everything turned on whether the witness saw my speech publicly or whether he got it from the state security. Footnote 3 confirms that this witness was coached on the basis of documents of the state security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No further intervention. Let's move on. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next footnote -- the next page, please, in this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And do we see there, Mr. Muracevic, reference -- the footnote 4?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is that the document relating to the 200 -- the petition of 215?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: That is that document. It's part of the documents that we found in the municipal building which were handed over to be preserved. That is that document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Not receiving the translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the footnote 4 as well as footnote 3 read by the witness so that the interpreters can translate them? Could the witness please read them out so they could be translated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Could you read footnote 4, Mr. Muracevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Footnote 4 states the archives of the institutes for the investigation of crimes against humanity and international law in Sarajevo, from now on referred to as AIIZ, number -- inventory number 31185, citizens of the village of Krivoglavci, municipality of Vogosca, to the president of the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and others, beginning, "Esteemed gentlemen." This is something that the population of the village of Krivoglavci sent by Serb inhabitants. It's a petition sent to the Municipal Assembly of Vogosca and many other addresses, including the president of the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Actually it's a document that I found in the building of the Vogosca Municipal Assembly, and that was handed over to the archives of the institute for them to keep the document, this petition.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly like to ask the witness just to read footnote number 3. He's read footnote 4. Let him read footnote 3 so that we can see what is the basis for the testimony of this witness, so that we can see whether he's testifying based on his own experience or on the basis of archival material that was provided to him. This witness is not testifying as an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, it's not -- but it's fair enough to ask the witness to read out footnote 3. Can we go back to page 32?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you read out note 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me just a couple of words about footnote 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland will come back to you if necessary. At this moment could you kindly read footnote 3 for our benefit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Footnote 3 states: "Bulletin for the state commission for gathering facts on war crimes on the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina" in -- for the text referred to as the bulletin number 7, February 1994, pages 3 and 4. This is a bulletin that was printed and it was available to the public.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic. No, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just 4, can we look at 4 just to see the year, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He read out and we can see it later. Ms. Sutherland, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can I have 65 ter number 90233 on the screen, please? Your Honours, I'm sorry, I don't have an English translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, do you recognise what's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. This is precisely the petition containing 215 signatures of citizens. Not only did I find the document in the municipal building, when we entered it in 1996, but as the secretary of the local commune, I was present at the municipal council meeting when this material was on the agenda before the conflict broke out in the Vogosca municipality. This is one of the first documents that the delegates or the deputies, I don't know how they were referred to at the time, of the Serbian Democratic Party at the time, submitted to the Municipal Assembly of Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour. If we can go to the second page, actually, just to -- so that the witness and the Court can -- and Mr. Karadzic can see the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the footnote 4 we saw before refers to this document, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I remember that footnote 4 does not bear a date, does it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, just an archive broad number of the institute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Are you tendering the excerpt of his book as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. We can see the archive broad number. The one that is in footnote 4 of the book with the broad number is what is in the stamp at the bottom of the document on page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you tendering both documents, the excerpt of his book?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's been read into the record, the relevant pages. I would leave it for Your Honours and -- but I seek to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, why don't you admit them both.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We will actually upload the cover page of the witness's book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we will give the numbers. We will mark that for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: About the book --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm having some problems, I apologise for this, but looking at the disclosure letter of the 13th of October, 2009, I don't find that the book is included there. It's 20 pages long and I'm looking quickly so maybe I missed it, and that's also a disclosure of materials relating to the death of individuals in Bosnia pursuant to a Rule 66(B) request. And if indeed the book was disclosed to us in that way, I don't think that that's really an adequate disclosure to prepare us to cross-examine this witness, and I'm going to ask, unfortunately, that we allow this witness or ask this witness to remain so that we could review the book this evening and, if necessary, put further questions to him tomorrow, unless there is a better showing of how this was called to our attention. It's our fault for missing it if that's the case, but we truly did -- all of us are seeing this for the first time and I don't doubt it was disclosed to us at some point, but somehow we didn't connect it with this witness and we're not -- we are just taken by surprise by the fact that there is some book written by this witness that we should have read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the index that was provided, it's -- the description is: "Book by Eset Muracevic in relation to events in Vogosca municipality between 1992 and 1995, presented to Stephen Margetts by Bilal Hasanovic [phoen]." So we gave the title of the book and the source of how we got the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And it was in 199-- in 2009.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 13th of October, 2009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I thought it would be in the interests of the Defence to admit that book but may I take it that you are opposed to admitting those two pages of the book?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we are. Simply because we don't feel we had adequate notice of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit the petition only. We mark it for identification. Pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2399, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also have the document that was referred to in footnote 3, but I don't think that that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's up to you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, yesterday Mr. Karadzic, at transcript page 12678, or 77, and again was talking about documents that -- that you had found in relation to the number of persons that were no longer living in the Vogosca municipality, and I offered the two documents yesterday to Mr. Karadzic as -- during his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 90230, and we apologise for the quality of this document in advance, Your Honour, of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document that's on the screen, Mr. Muracevic?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is a decision appointing a municipal commission for the 1993 census and the -- it's being issued by the chairman of the Executive Board of Vogosca municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And as a result of that decision, a further document that you referred to yesterday was produced.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 90231 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise what -- that document?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recognise this document. This is an excerpt of listed inhabitants living in the areas controlled by the local Serbs relating to this decision to form this commission, census commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is the first results -- the first results for the Ticisko [phoen] districts and hamlets and it's dated the 17th of June, 1993. You said that there were no inhabitants of Svrake left in the municipality at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 in the B/C/S and page 2 also of the English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a remark. This is not an official census but this is a list made by the municipality of those villages that were accessible to it. So that it could carry out a social policy, that it could provide services to the inhabitants. This is a list of persons who are living there and those who have moved there in order to be able to provide them with benefits, but there are villages where it was not possible to go but that doesn't mean that there is nobody living in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that comment was unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're not giving evidence and, if necessary, after the re-examination, you may ask for further cross-examination. The way how you intervene during the course of re-examination is not helpful today. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we can see, Mr. Muracevic, can we not, for the village of Svrake, that there are no Muslims residing there as of June 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, you can see that there were no Muslims there. Svrake was under the control of the local Serbs. They could have gone in. They were in control of it, in that area, in that period. All these settlements that are referred to in this list were under full control of the Serbian authorities. Each one of these hamlets and villages could be accessed by them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document and I also seek to tender the document 90230 which -- which is the decision of Koprica which, in fact, says: "Pursuant to conclusions from the 70th session of the government of the Republika Srpska, a committee will be formed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did we have the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, both of them will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P2400 and 2401, respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm sorry about this. We are dealing with some exhibits that we're really not familiar with, but if you could go back to the petition, 90233, the 65 ter number, that was -- you've admitted, I'm wondering when that was disclosed to us because in look -- if you could call that up and look at it on your screen, I think it would be useful --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, that -- sorry. We obtained that document this morning at around -- whatever the fax header says on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think that should have been noted. First of all, they needed permission to add it to the Rule 65 ter list. We just noticed it ourselves when we were looking at it. It's a fax -- it's the 2nd of March, 2011. Otherwise we were under the impression that this was a document that had been part of the 2 million pages that have been disclosed to us sometime within the last few years. Now we find out that it was -- it's been offered without any motion to add it to the 65 ter list. It's never been disclosed to us. I think that it ought to be withdrawn from admission as a sanction for this kind of way of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is re-examination, not examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The petition was specifically mentioned during the course of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was, but this is a document that hasn't been disclosed to us before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I'm sorry to intervene --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's leave it. Let me consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, can you tell us, this document, would you have been taken ex improviso by this, by surprise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we are taken by surprise by this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: You have been, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This petition was raised during the course of cross-examination and we are of the view that the Prosecution is entitled to present this document, and if necessary, the Defence is allowed to put further questions about this document, given the timing of this disclosure. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, it's the Prosecution position that documents used in re-examination don't need to be disclosed to the Defence prior to being used in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Prior to -- prior to being used, just before you start the re-examination. I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. President, just so that we are on the same page in case this arises again. Just as we do when we start the cross-examination, we e-mail a list of all the documents we intend to use, so at the very latest the Prosecution should disclose at the commencement of the re-examination these documents, not that it would have made much difference but I understand that would be the procedure for disclosure on re-examination. If the document has not previously been disclosed to us, then at the time the re-examination commences, an e-mail should be sent to us and the Chamber in which the list of documents to be used in re-examination are disclosed. Wouldn't that be could be consistent with the same principles that we operate under for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but re-examination comes as a result of cross-examination, and you know, we are doing this on the fly, and if we -- something that is said five minutes before the end of the cross-examination, we react to it by getting a document and putting it to the witness in a certain circumstance. And I think that by putting this -- what is requested by Mr. Robinson is wholly unnecessary and unworkable.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say a word?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I -- not this time, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I have the right to respond to what Ms. Sutherland said with regard to cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I said no, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, the Prosecution is entitled to use documents which was not listed on the 65 ter list, if that topic is triggered by the cross-examination. And not because of the timing of this disclosure of this document, but newness of the content to the Defence, we will allow the Defence to put questions, if necessary, on that basis. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the newness of the content of this document, it's not new information. We have other -- another exhibit, for example, which has information along the same lines as this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber was of the view that -- Defence was not in the position to know the content of this petition.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did I ask -- then I will be granted additional time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Only in relation to this petition. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
