utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, following on from the decision pursuant to a conclusion of the government of Republika Srpska to set up the census committee and then the results of the census committee in June 1993, you then went on in your testimony yesterday to talk about 13.157 people being expelled from the municipality. And Mr. Karadzic asked you about that figure and where you got that figure from and you said that, you know, you had the documents and that you had brought the documents with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 90232 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I compiled it by comparing the official census numbers in Bosnia-Herzegovina from 1991 and the census conducted in June 1993, by the Serbian authorities in the territory under their control. By making these comparisons, I included only the settlements that they listed and that they -- that were under their control.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And when you say the documents listed in their document, that's the document that we have just seen, the 17th of June, 1993, document?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about these very documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to object. This witness is not a demographic expert or any expert at all. He is an eyewitness. Therefore, I need additional time for cross-examination. Here we have elements and data introduced herein that were not comprised by the testimony of this witness. And in addition to that, I feel that I have been ambushed because there are things that I am not aware of and that I wasn't warned about. I'm talking about the book, the petition and the REST of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karadzic was querying with the witness where he was coming up with this figure of 13.157. This is simply to show that the witness compiled this document from the Serb figures against the 1991 census figures. And the 1991 census figures is 65 ter number 00242.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this is part of the document he brought.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He brought this document and it was disclosed to the Defence on Sunday. I seek to tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This is handwriting by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't see any problem in admitting this but shall we mark it for identification? Or is it unnecessary?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, on Monday evening, and this is an expert work produced by this witness. This is a document that we are looking at. And I received it on Monday night. It was disclosed to me after I returned from the court on Monday night.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it doesn't take an expert to compile a chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The weight of this document is to be decided by the Chamber later on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can just take the witness to the second, third and fourth pages. Just -- sorry, I should have done that before I sought to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, can you just explain to the Court what is on the second, third and fourth pages, please?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the results of the census, the 1991 official census carried out in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it refers to the entire Vogosca municipality. Listed here are the villages and settlements that were also the subject of the census carried out by the Serbian authorities in 1993. So by comparing the figures from the official census and the figures that they reached, we got the numbers that were mentioned in the previous document. This is an integral part of this document. It is the structure of Vogosca municipality divided into villages and settlements, and the number of residents per nationality that lived in 1991 in those settlements and villages. Specifically, if we speak about my local commune of Svrake, that's the fourth row from the top, there used to be 1.245 residents; Muslims, 1.036; 170 Serbs; two Croats; 21, the others -- Yugoslavs and the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That information is already on the record. Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's safer to mark it for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2402, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The number is 2400, 2400?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI P2402.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 02. If necessary, Mr. Karadzic, as we indicated, we will allow you to put questions in relation to the petition, the document we saw previously.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I would also like to ask questions regarding the census, because this was not mentioned in examination-in-chief. I just have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, did you find this document in Vogosca municipality building in 1996? I'm talking about the petition.

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Accused, I found this document in 1996 when we arrived in Vogosca. However, that was not the first time that I saw that document. I had seen it much earlier because as a secretary of the local commune, I attended meetings of the Vogosca Municipal Assembly and I had an opportunity to be in the municipal building when this petition was discussed and was on the agenda of the meeting, which is before the 1992 conflict broke out. So that was in the period after the multi-party elections and 1991. I cannot remember exactly which session that was, and on which date it was held. However, I did see this document before, and as a secretary of the local commune, I did not only see it, I would regularly receive materials for the Assembly meetings, and as part of the materials that I received for these -- ahead of these sessions I saw this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, after the adjournment of this Court, who did you talk to?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, after the adjournment? What are you talking about? Are you talking about the courthouse or somewhere in town?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who did you discuss this document with today in order to obtain it?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not talk to anyone. I suppose that the Prosecutor -- I personally did not talk to anyone about obtaining this document. However, since the place of custody of this document is mentioned in the footnote of my book, I suppose that it was the Prosecution who received the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Somebody should have been called at the institute and ordered this document to be delivered.

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me something that I was not in a position to do anything about. I did not contact anyone in Sarajevo yesterday, particularly not in -- with a view to obtaining a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this document was in public domain in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the petition was being mentioned. However, I can't say whether it was published in any of the media. Looking at the number of the addresses that it was sent to, I think that it was in the public domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this is not the original, because there is a note which says that the original petition is being kept by the secretary of the Republican Assembly and it can be reviewed if necessary. Do you have the date of this petition? And there must be the date on the original, on the incoming stamp when it was received by the BH Assembly.

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: As a secretary of the local commune, I received copies of the material that was being sent to all the deputies that were in the municipal council. So I did not receive the original that was received by the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was anyway not necessary for me to get the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what is the connection that you establish between this and my information relating to my conversation with Izetbegovic concerning your quotation?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not establish any link between this petition and your conversation with Mr. Izetbegovic. It was mentioned only in the context of your fiery speeches delivered with regard to the plebiscite, when you specifically and personally said that in the areas that were going to be under the Serb control, no sale of land would be allowed to Muslims or the construction of any residential facilities by the Muslims in the Serb-controlled areas. I also quoted the portion in which you said that each foundation made by Muslims would be blown up in those territories and the petition itself was mentioned in the sense that in a certain way, representatives of the Serbian Democratic Party who were on the municipal council, one of the documents that was presented at the joint session which was attended by the Serbs and Muslims alike, they were requesting the ban on the sale of land by the Serbs to the Muslims, and not to have them building houses in that village. So this is the relation that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You don't know the date, but do you know if I ever said this publicly or was it a document that was relating to a party meeting?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: By reading the footnote and I think I provided the -- an explanation of where this quotation came from, what the source was, and this portion that I quoted as your words, I made a reference to a document that was publicly published in the bulletin, which is mentioned in one of the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karadzic put the very same question to the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you've exhausted with this. We will allow you one or two questions about the census. Just one or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At least one question relating to the census. Mr. Muracevic, was the sentence that I said, did it refer to the local Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought your ruling was that he could ask questions in relation to the petition only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no. During the course -- when he raised the question, we discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But my apology not to have asked you, but we agreed to allow him to put questions in relation to that census, one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Muracevic, what I said to my party colleagues in relation to my conversation with Mr. Izetbegovic, did it refer to the ban on the purchase of land by the local Muslims or did it refer to the land that was intended to be sold to Turkish immigrants that would alter the demographic composition of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't know what you meant when you said "Muslims." Whenever you said "Muslims," I understood that to mean all the citizens of that ethnicity. I cannot guess, second guess, what you had in mind because I didn't have an opportunity to hear what you really meant. When you said Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How is that question related to that census? Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I was raising it for that reason, Your Honour. In fact, this question doesn't relate to the census. It goes back again to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that I was entitled to two questions about the petition and the census respectively. That's why I wanted to ask whether this document shows what I actually said to Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then I think -- do you have any further questions with respect to that census we saw?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, tell me this: During the war, were any Muslims in the following villages, Hotonj, Kamenica, Kobilja Glava, Perca, Tihovici, Ugljesici, and Ugorsko, and I'll stop there. Were the Muslims living in those villages throughout the whole war?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, your question goes beyond the census and the documents that we saw because the census that was compiled by the Serbian authorities --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: Parts of Kobilja Glava and some of these settlements were under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and, yes, Muslims indeed lived there. However, the question of comparing the 1991 census and the 1993 census and the figures contained there took into account only parts of the settlements that were under the Serbian control, and not the territory that was under the control of the BH Army. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Don't argue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, were these boxes left blank, although they were on the list? So everything was left blank as if nobody lived in those villages?

utterances.speaker: ESET MURACEVIC (Resumed]
utterances.text: I would really like to see this document again, where the summary is shown. So in the villages that you controlled, before actually they came under your control, a certain number of Muslims, Croats and the others used to live, Yugoslavs and other ethnicities. So in my village, in Svrake, 1.036 Muslims lived; whereas in the 1993 census, made by the Serbian authorities, it is shown that there was not a single Muslim living in that village anymore. The village of Tihovici was 100 per cent Muslim, and in 1991 there were 367 Muslims living there, while your census takers, in 1993, did not find a single Muslim there, and they couldn't find them there because on the 4th of July, this village was attacked by the Army of Republika Srpska and killed over 30 residents of the village and expelled the rest of them. So these are comparative indicators of the situation in the villages and places that you held under your control, and it also shows that before you gained control of these territories, a certain number of Muslims used to live. So these are the territories that were exclusively under the control of the Serbian army. And in 1991, there were 11.331 Muslims, whereas in 1993 there were only 210 of them. There were 660 Croats, and in 1993, there were 302. And as for the rest, Yugoslavs and other ethnicities, accounted for 1.098 in 1991, and in 1993, your census taker registered only 239 members of this group. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's more than sufficient. Let's conclude here. As for the -- Mr. Robinson's request to ask the witness to remain until tomorrow to be asked further questions about his book, given the timing of the disclosure, we find it necessary and we do not grant -- we deny that motion, if that is a motion. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Muracevic. Thank you for your indulgence and thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm wondering whether there is any point to bring in the next witness. I leave it in your hands, Mr. Tieger or Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm looking at the clock. I think we've only got six minutes left. It's probably not worth beginning today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We didn't progress very well today. Thanks to the indulgence of the court staff and the interpreters and the stenographers. We -- as indicated, we would be able to sit tomorrow five 1-hour sessions, from 9 until 3.15. And next week, Mr. Tieger, it seems implausible to sit for an extended hours, given the court schedule. There is a -- another trial in the afternoon. Well, tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of March, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.23 p.m.,
